detail.body:
(#8824 should be merged first)

In #8770, we pinned Modal sandbox placement to Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI), where a working NVIDIA driver version was still available, to avoid the CUDA/NCCL failures seen on other Modal hosts.
The affected driver has since been rolled out to OCI as well, so this workaround no longer provides a reliable path for our multi-GPU CI workload. Modal has identified the issue and is working on a fix.

This PR temporarily disables Modal until the driver issue is resolved, and run the required torch-latest workflow entirely on the existing AWS backend.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Gate cleanup on successful AWS authentication**

If `collect-tests` fails, the deploy job is deliberately admitted by its job-level condition and `Fail if test selection failed` exits before the checkout and AWS-auth steps. This unconditional `always()` nevertheless runs `python3 ci/torch_latest.py cleanup-aws`, so the script is absent and credentials were never exported, creating a second unrelated failure instead of the intended selector error; checkout, setup, artifact-download, and auth failures have the same problem. Give the auth step an id and mirror the smoke job's `steps.aws-auth.outcome == 'success'` guard so reconciliation still runs whenever allocation could have begun.

After this AWS-only path lands, `.github/workflows/TEST_SELECTION.md:7-8`, `:28-36`, and `:396-434` still describe Modal-first execution, a Modal smoke job, and OIDC credentials acquired only after a Modal capacity result, while `CONTRIBUTING.md:55-57` still says this conserves Modal quota. Since this workflow explicitly links that document as its trust/security model, maintainers will follow incorrect credential and smoke/troubleshooting instructions during the temporary mode; update those sections or clearly document the temporary override with this switch.
